findings.issue: KEPT_TREE_FORCE understates what the named `git worktree remove --force` destroys. It lists uncommitted, untracked and ignored files and 'each submodule checked out in it', but removing the worktree also deletes git's record directory, so commits that live only in a submodule repository under that record's modules/ directory are lost. This is the very data the task's own case ta11 proves a redo keeps. The tree's detached HEAD commits also become unreachable unless pinned. The tail 'carry what it holds first' does not tell the reader to look for either. Confirmed from the code: the text is the whole warning and mentions neither.
findings.resolution: Extend KEPT_TREE_FORCE to say it also deletes git's record of the tree, so commits held only in a checked-out submodule's repository and the tree's detached HEAD (if no ref holds it) are lost. Pin kt5 on those words.

findings.issue: With the plan unreadable (task_ids None) the new `_kept_tree_remedy` names `git worktree remove --force` for EVERY kept tree, including a blocked member's tree that close_wave records under its task id (drive-phase.py:5936-5941) and that a later wave adopts by marker. Before the diff, a None plan gave the bare remover, which refuses a tree holding work. Now the one case where status cannot tell a task's tree from a kept old tree gets the destructive command. Confirmed: the only guard is `task_ids is not None and task_id in task_ids`.
findings.resolution: When task_ids is None, name the safe form (bare `git worktree remove <path>`, or say the plan could not be read and the key cannot be classified) and give the forced form only for a key matching the ` set aside <n>` shape (drive-phase.py _ASIDE_KEY_RE). Add a case for the unreadable-plan row.

findings.issue: The claim 'a path once taken is never cut at again' is stronger than the code. RECUTS is a dict keyed by task id and is not in KEPT_AT_TASK_CLOSE (line 905), so the generic loop at drive-phase.py:8673-8676 pops recuts[task] when the task closes. drop_state removes the whole file when the phase finishes. After that, if every kept tree has been removed, the high-water mark is gone and a later redo can start again at .redo-1. The lexists and git-listing checks stop it landing on a path that still exists, so no tree is overwritten, but a removed path can be reused. ta20b only proves the claim while the recuts entry is present.
findings.resolution: Either soften the guide and docstring to 'never cut at a path that still holds a directory or a git record', or add RECUTS to KEPT_AT_TASK_CLOSE and state that the mark ends with the phase.

findings.issue: keep_old_tree picks the next key from state['keptTrees'] alone. A tree whose marker already names '<id> set aside <n>' but whose state entry is gone (drop_state at finish, or a forgotten entry) is not seen, so the key can be issued twice, and settle_kept_markers would then read the older tree's marker as a crash of the new redo. Confirmed from the code; reachable only after the state was lost.
findings.resolution: Also skip a key some wave tree's marker already names, or skip any key whose entry was ever recorded under recuts.

findings.issue: submit_tree reads wave.trees directly and never calls settle_kept_markers, which runs only in drive_locked. A submit that arrives after a redo died between the marker rewrite and the state write is keyed to the old tree, whose marker already names the kept key. Confirmed: no other caller of the settle.
findings.resolution: Call settle_kept_markers (or the marker read) in submit_tree before it resolves the tree, or document that submit is refused until the next drive step.

findings.issue: The sweep's reason for a kept tree says 'the wave driver removes it with `task-remove` after integration', which is false for a kept old tree (its key is no task, and task-remove refuses it). The task's own list named this reader (the sweep's kept-tree reason in _worktrees.py); the executor checked it, called the wording wrong and left it. The sweep is path-agnostic and still keeps the tree, so no work is at risk, but it is the one remedy surface left naming a verb that cannot act on a kept old tree.
findings.resolution: Make the reason depend on whether the marker's taskId is a ` set aside <n>` key, and for that case name `git worktree remove --force <path>` or the driver's retire.

preExisting.issue: drop_state at finish deletes the whole drive-state file, so keptTrees entries (and the recuts record) for trees still standing are forgotten and status stops listing them. This predates the diff; the kept trees remain registered worktrees.
preExisting.resolution: Carry keptTrees across the phase's end, or name the remaining trees on the finish did-line.

intent.note: Clause 'Redesign so the redo moves nothing': keep_old_tree rewrites only the marker (whole-or-nothing via write_record) and then record_kept writes the state; there is no rename, lock, repair or repoint left, and the diff deletes set_aside_tree, repair_asides, _settle_move, asideMoves, _git_floor, ASIDE_REMEDY and the STATE_WRITERS row. A grep over the tree (outside docs/audit) for the removed names found none. 'new tree at a fresh path beside it': add_tree calls recut_path, which cuts at <first tree>.redo-<n> past the high-water mark, any directory and any git-listed path; wave.trees then names it. 'State where a second and third redo cut': the guide names .redo-1, .redo-2, .redo-3, and ta20 pins them. 'Settle a crash by the marker': settle_kept_markers in drive_locked, pinned by ta21. 'Check every reader of wave.trees and tree_path': listed in the outcome. retire_member, close_wave and submit_tree are path-agnostic; task-add adopts by marker regardless of path (manage-worktrees.py do_task_add), so a recut tree at .redo-1 is adopted correctly by a later wave. 'name what works for the remedy and say what --force deletes' is met with the gaps in findings 1 and 2. Two clauses are met only in part: the 'never reused' statement is stronger than the code (finding 3), and the sweep reader was listed but its wording left wrong (finding 6). The executor's claim describes the diff accurately. I did not re-run the 15-row mutation probe or the 1712 s gate; their figures are unverified by me. test_audit_status.py (kt5, kt6, kt6b) is not in tests.gate, so the recorded gate run does not cover those cases.
